transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello — do you have any questions about your cataract surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You can go back to light exercise after 1 week, and that includes gardening. Just avoid heavy lifting or strenuous work for 1 month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that information. I also wanted to ask when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Yes, it’s safe to continue using any eye drops you were using before your operation, including for dry eyes, unless you were told otherwise.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's good to hear. Another thing I've noticed is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Some sensitivity to light can be normal while your eyes adjust, and if things just seem brighter than usual, wearing sunglasses outside is recommended.

But significant pain in bright light, or severe light sensitivity, is not normal, especially if the eye is also red and painful, and this may need to be checked further.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for clarifying that. One last question: should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text:
Some mild blurriness can be common right after surgery as your eye continues to heal and adjust, but usually it should gradually improve. If you experience persistent or worsening blurriness, it would be worth following up with your doctor to make sure everything is healing properly.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Yes — it’s common for vision not to be completely clear in the first week after surgery. It should improve quickly and settle down over time.

If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all the questions I had. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have all your questions been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they have. Thanks again for your assistance!
